name: Raynham
blurb: Raynham and the surrounding Route 44 corridor are home to a dense mix of home service businesses competing for the same searches. We've built websites and CRM systems for HVAC and contracting companies based right in town.
featuredWork: Most of our Raynham work has centered on HVAC and mechanical contractors — building out a CRM that tracks recurring maintenance contracts, not just one-off installs, and a website built to win the "AC repair near me" searches that spike every July.

name: Lynn
blurb: Lynn's mix of dense residential neighborhoods and older housing stock keeps hardscaping, tree service, and remodeling crews busy year-round — and makes local search visibility especially competitive.
featuredWork: For hardscaping and tree crews in Lynn, the win is usually a photo-first website — before/after project galleries load fast and rank locally — paired with a CRM that keeps estimates from falling through the cracks during the spring rush.

name: Rehoboth
blurb: Rehoboth's larger residential lots make it a strong market for hardscaping, patios, and outdoor living projects — the kind of work that sells on photos and a fast-loading project gallery.
featuredWork: Rehoboth's larger properties mean bigger-ticket hardscape and patio projects — so the sites we build here lean hard on visual proof of work and a lead form built to pre-qualify project size before the first phone call.

name: South Yarmouth
blurb: Cape Cod's seasonal population swings mean local service businesses in South Yarmouth need marketing that ramps up ahead of summer and a CRM that keeps second-home clients on the books year after year.
featuredWork: Painting and remodeling crews on this stretch of Cape Cod deal with a hard seasonal calendar — we build marketing that ramps ahead of the summer rush and a CRM that keeps second-home owners on the books year after year instead of starting from zero each spring.

name: Plymouth
blurb: Plymouth's mix of historic homes and new construction keeps carpentry, painting, and remodeling contractors busy with two very different kinds of projects — and two very different kinds of customers to market to.
featuredWork: Plymouth's split between historic-home restoration and new-construction finish work means the carpentry and remodeling businesses we work with here usually need two distinct pitches on one site — we build the pages and CRM pipelines to keep both leads separated and followed up on correctly.

name: Northborough
blurb: Northborough sits at the center of a MetroWest market with strong demand for both residential and commercial glass and glazing work, from storefront installs to custom shower enclosures.
featuredWork: Glass and glazing work in Northborough splits between commercial storefront bids and residential shower/mirror installs — we build separate service pages and CRM pipelines for each, since a $40,000 storefront job and a $600 shower enclosure need completely different follow-up.

name: Harwich
blurb: Harwich's classic-car and craftsman community supports specialty trades that sell on reputation and visible quality of work — exactly the kind of business a portfolio-driven website is built for.
featuredWork: Classic car and restoration shops in Harwich sell almost entirely on visible craftsmanship, so the sites we build here are portfolio-first — high-resolution project galleries and a CRM built around long, relationship-driven restoration timelines instead of quick one-off jobs.

name: Rockland
blurb: Rockland and the surrounding South Shore towns are steady territory for masonry and hardscape contractors, with enough new construction and renovation work to keep a well-marketed crew booked solid.
featuredWork: Masonry crews around Rockland run on steady South Shore renovation and new-construction demand — the sites and CRM systems we build here are focused on turning estimate requests into a real scheduled pipeline instead of a pile of unanswered texts.

name: Beverly
blurb: Beverly and the North Shore combine coastal weather exposure with older housing stock — a market where masonry, exterior, and restoration businesses stay busy if they can be found by the right searches.
featuredWork: Coastal weather exposure keeps masonry, gutter, and exterior-restoration businesses on the North Shore busy — the challenge in Beverly is usually just being found first, so we lean on local service pages and review-driven marketing to win that first call.

name: Derry
blurb: Derry anchors a fast-growing corner of southern New Hampshire where masonry, tree work, and remodeling businesses are competing against a wave of new residents searching for local contractors online for the first time.
featuredWork: Derry's growth means a wave of new residents searching for a local contractor for the first time — the masonry, tree, and remodeling businesses we work with here win by showing up first in those searches and following up fast enough to lock in the job before a competitor calls back.
